NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)  
Proposed intervention: a coordinated three-axis parameter/procedure change — (1) VFD dv/dt limiting enabled and switching frequency reduced to the motor-nameplate minimum, (2) termination/gland sealing upgraded to a double-seal anaerobic-thread-sealant procedure with calibrated torque sequence, (3) pump duty-cycle scheduled to run only when well level is below 50 % of the cable’s submerged length — all implemented on existing equipment without new hardware.  
Standard practice: sets VFD switching frequency to a default (e.g., 4 kHz) without dv/dt limiting, uses a single-seal gland procedure, and runs the pump on a level-based on/off cycle that energizes the cable at all submerged lengths.  
Departure: the novelty is the **simultaneous, quantified retuning of all three permitted axes** to attack the water-tree driving variables (electric-field stress and moisture-exposure time) as a single mechanism; standard practice treats them independently and does not minimize dv/dt via software.  
Adjacent-technique clearance: the closest existing mitigation in any industry is installing external dv/dt filters or sine-wave filters (hardware). This intervention achieves comparable dv/dt reduction and stress-cycle reduction purely through VFD parameter retuning, sealing procedure upgrade, and scheduling — a genuine departure because it uses no added components.

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: water-tree growth rate ∝ Eⁿ·t (n≈2–3), where E is the peak electric field in the insulation and t is the energized time under moisture. VFD dv/dt determines the voltage overshoot at the cable end (ΔV ∝ dv/dt·√(L·C)), which directly raises E. Switching frequency f_sw determines the number of stress cycles per second (t_eff ∝ f_sw·t_on). Submerged cable length L_sub determines the defect population exposed to moisture while energized.  
Magnitude verification: enabling VFD dv/dt limit (typical minimum 200 V/µs vs. default 1000–2000 V/µs) reduces ΔV by ~60–80 %, cutting E by a similar factor; reducing f_sw from 4 kHz to 1.5 kHz cuts stress cycles by 62 %; scheduling to run only when L_sub < 50 % cuts exposed defect length by ≥50 %. Combined effect reduces the growth-rate driver by >90 % (0.2·0.38·0.5 ≈ 0.038).  
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = peak electric-field stress (E) and energized moisture-exposure time (t); the mechanism moves E **down** by limiting dv/dt and moves t **down** by lowering f_sw and restricting energized submerged length; this **reduces** the water-tree growth rate.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
| # | Component / Action | Generic Class / Stated Item | Attachment Point in Stated Infrastructure | Operating Parameter / Procedure Detail | Tag |
|---|-------------------|----------------------------|------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-----|
| 1 | VFD dv/dt limit enable | Existing VFD (stated) | VFD parameter menu (existing control) | Set “dv/dt limit” or “soft PWM” to minimum available value (e.g., 200 V/µs) | (c) |
| 2 | VFD switching frequency reduction | Existing VFD (stated) | VFD parameter menu (existing control) | Set switching frequency to motor-nameplate minimum (e.g., 1.5 kHz) | (c) |
| 3 | Termination/gland sealing procedure | Existing cable glands (stated) | Motor-terminal box and well-head gland (existing) | Apply anaerobic thread sealant (standard catalog, e.g., Loctite 545 equivalent) to gland threads; torque gland nuts to manufacturer spec in two stages (50 % then 100 %) with 5 min dwell; inspect seal visually | (c) |
| 4 | Duty-cycle scheduling logic | Existing pump controller & well-level sensor (stated) | Pump control system (existing PLC/relay logic) | Modify start/stop logic: pump runs only when well-level sensor reads < 50 % of cable submerged length; hysteresis band ±5 % to prevent chatter | (c) |

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
| Burden Category | Standard Practice | This Intervention | Comparison |
|-----------------|-------------------|-------------------|------------|
| Hardware procurement | None (uses existing VFD, glands, controller) | None (all rows (c)) | Same |
| Installation labor | Standard gland sealing (single seal, no torque sequence) | Enhanced gland sealing (double seal, torque sequence) | +15 min per gland (2 glands) — negligible, same skill level |
| Commissioning | VFD default parameters; level-based on/off | VFD parameter changes (2 settings); scheduling logic update | +30 min engineering time — same tooling (laptop/keypad) |
| Operational loss | Continuous pumping per level | Pumping restricted to L_sub < 50 % | **Zero net loss**: scheduling shifts pumping to lower-level windows; total daily volume unchanged (pump runs longer when level is low). Explicitly priced at 0 kWh/day. |
| Maintenance | Periodic gland inspection | Same inspection frequency; sealant is standard catalog item | Same |
| Cost class | No added cost | No added cost (sealant is standard catalog, <$10) | Same or lower |

Conclusion: same-or-lower burden class in every row; no hidden development, machining, or custom parts.

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol:  
1. Baseline: install a portable partial-discharge (PD) monitor (high-frequency CT on cable ground conductor, 100 MHz bandwidth) for 7 days of normal operation. Record PD pulse count, magnitude (mV), and phase-resolved pattern.  
2. Intervention: apply all four bill rows (VFD parameters, sealing procedure, scheduling).  
3. Post-intervention: repeat PD monitoring for 7 days under similar well-level cycles.  
Instruments: portable PD monitor (standard catalog, e.g., HV Diagnostics PD-Surveyor class), laptop.  
Pass/fail thresholds:  
- PD pulse count reduced by ≥50 % (same voltage phase windows).  
- Maximum PD magnitude reduced by ≥40 %.  
- No new PD activity at termination phase angles (validates sealing).  
Duration: 14 days total (7 baseline + 7 post).  
Kill criterion: if PD count or magnitude increases, or if motor torque becomes insufficient at 1.5 kHz (trip on overload), revert VFD parameters and declare intervention falsified.
